title: Stealing Training Graphs from Graph Neural Networks

problem.claim: Training graphs may leak from trained GNN parameters, creating a privacy risk when trained models are shared.

gap.claim: Explorations into training-data leakage from trained GNNs are limited.

contributions.claim: A graph diffusion model with diffusion-noise optimization is used to generate high-quality graphs resembling the target training set.
A selection method uses GNN model parameters to identify training graphs among graphs generated by the diffusion model.
Theoretical analysis connects trained GNN parameters with the training graphs used.

stated_novelty.claim: The paper investigates the novel problem of stealing graphs from trained GNNs.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Results on real-world datasets show that the framework can extract training graphs from trained GNNs.

narrative_sequence.summary: GNNs are used to model graphs across various tasks.
Specialized GNN training requires costly and sensitive expert annotations, while shared model parameters may leak private training data.
Theoretical analysis links trained GNN parameters to training graphs, but prior exploration of this leakage is limited.
The framework generates candidate graphs with diffusion-noise optimization and selects likely training graphs using GNN parameters.
Experiments on real-world datasets report framework effectiveness.

unknowns: Datasets, baselines, metrics, and quantitative results
Defenses and conditions under which leakage may fail
